newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Gunmen kill two Pakistani Shi'ite leaders.
newsitem.headline: Gunmen kill two Pakistani Shi'ite leaders.

text.p: Gunmen on motorcycles killed two Pakistani Shi'ite Moslem sect leaders and four other people on Tuesday in ambushes of their vehicles in two cities of the central province of Punjab, police said.

Zulfikar Naqvi, provincial vice-president of the Shi'ite Tehrik-i-Jafaria party, his son Hamaad Naqvi and their driver died instantly after five unidentified gunmen fired Kalashnikov assault rifles at them in the provincial capital Lahore.
A friend of the elder Naqvi and a police guard accompanying them in the car died later in hospital, police said.
A local Shi'ite leader, Mohammad Ayub Siddiqi, was killed by two masked gunmen on a motorcyle later at night in the main southern Punjab town of Multan, the police there said.
That attack followed a march by Shi'ite activists in Multan to protest against the Lahore shooting.
Police said they had no immediate information about the identity of the gunmen or the motives.
Three days ago, unknown gunmen killed the provincial ombudsman in Lahore, retired Supreme Court judge Munir Ahmad Khan.

But Tehrik-i-Jafaria, representing the minority Shi'ite sect, and its rival Sipah-i-Sahaba Pakistan militant group from the majority Sunni sect have often accused each other of attacking their activists and mosques.
The official APP news agency quoted a senior police official in Lahore as saying the police had yet to determine whether Tuesday's killings were the result of a sectarian clash.
Police said on Monday they had arrested the chief of the Shi'ite militant group Sipah-i-Mohammad, Ghulam Raza Naqvi, and recovered 12 rocket launchers from him.

Sunni-Shi'ite disputes over Islamic beliefs have often spilled into violence in Pakistan, and there has been a wave of such incidents in recent months in Punjab and North West Frontier province in which scores of people have died.
Sunnis dominate Pakistan's population of about 130 million, of which Shi'ites constitute about 15 percent.
